conditions: For the modelled Indonesian citizen without an independently established entry/residence exemption, section6(3) requires the normally pre-entry national visa for a longer-term purpose. Indonesia is not among section41(1) onshore-application nationalities. Other individual lawful exemptions or unreviewed purposes are not denied.

The academic skilled-worker purpose under sections18(2)-(3) and18b requires a recognised or comparable degree, a specific qualified-job offer, actual intended employment, professional permission where required and employment-agency approval where applicable. The Embassy Jakarta academic-worker application route supports a real procedure, not an ordinary resident already meeting these conditions.

General section5 identity, passport, livelihood and absence-of-expulsion conditions remain, with adequate health insurance under section2(3). First section18a/18b permits after age45 normally require the statutory salary or adequate retirement provision, subject to exceptions. No origin-median-income qualification or annual salary amount is inferred.

Original documents, biometrics, fees and an individual decision remain necessary. National entry visas and subsequent residence titles are distinct; section4a employment permission remains. No approval rate, job, affordability, asset transfer, transport or crisis connectivity is established. Indonesian citizenship is an explicit profile assumption, not inferred from geographic residence. No OPT score follows.
Valid identity document and qualifying free-movement status; no visa or residence title required for Union citizens.
Workers have a residence path; job-seeking is limited to six months unless continued search and genuine hiring prospects are demonstrated.
Non-employed citizens require sufficient resources and health insurance; compliance can be checked and the right can be lost. Public-order, security and health restrictions remain.
EU citizenship or equivalent status under L200-3; valid identity document and public-order requirements.
Residence beyond three months requires professional activity, or sufficient resources and health insurance; this is not unconditional long-term residence.
The official worker guidance says no residence title is required, while regulated professions and certain public jobs have conditions.

Section 41(1) allows visa-free entry also for a non-short stay and an application for the required residence title from within Germany. This is a procedural application route, not automatic permission for long-term residence or employment. British nationality must satisfy the referenced FreizuegG/EU section 1(2)(6) definition; residence or a territorial code does not establish this status.
The required residence title must be applied for within 90 days of entry; expulsion or a shortened stay may end the deadline earlier. Section 41(4) excludes ICT-card applications from this route.

A qualifying residence purpose and its substantive conditions remain necessary. General section 5 conditions usually include secured livelihood, adequate health insurance under section 2(3), identity, passport and absence of expulsion grounds; median income at origin does not prove these conditions.

The reviewed academic skilled-worker example under sections 18 and 18b requires a recognised or comparable degree, a specific qualified-job offer, required professional permission and employment-agency approval where applicable. First section 18a/18b permits after age 45 normally require the statutory salary level or adequate retirement provision, subject to stated exceptions. Do not assume the ordinary resident qualifies.
Visa-free entry and filing an application do not by themselves authorise employment under section 4a. No processing time, job availability, resident affordability or crisis operation is established.

For the modelled Chinese citizen without an independently established entry/residence exemption, section6(3) provides a national visa for a longer-term residence purpose, normally issued before entry. China is not among section41(1) onshore-application nationalities; this is not a visa-free or tourist-to-work permission claim. Other lawful individual exemptions and unreviewed routes are not denied.

The reviewed academic skilled-worker residence purpose under sections18(2)-(3) and18b requires a recognised or comparable degree, a specific qualified-job offer, actual intended employment, professional permission where required and employment-agency approval where applicable. Do not assume ordinary residents meet these conditions.

General section5 conditions normally include secured livelihood, identity, passport and absence of expulsion grounds; adequate health insurance is included in section2(3). First section18a/18b permits after age45 normally require the statutory salary level or adequate retirement provision, subject to stated exceptions. No annual salary amount or origin-median-income eligibility is inferred.

Section4a employment permission and title restrictions remain. A legal conditional application/residence purpose is not an issued visa, job, actual approval rate, affordable relocation, transferable assets, transport redundancy or crisis connectivity. Chinese citizenship is an explicit model assumption, not inferred from geographic residence; HKG/MAC/TWN and foreign residents do not inherit CHN here.
